stem:
Meera's teacher asks her to compare how animals digest food. She reads: 'A cow brings partly digested grass back to its mouth and chews it again; a bird's gizzard has muscular walls that contract and relax, often with grit, to grind food.'
Meera must decide whether each statement below correctly describes an adaptation that is different from human chewing.
• The cow's cud chewing is an adaptation different from human chewing.
• The gizzard's grinding action is an adaptation different from human chewing.
Which row is correct?
cud chewing gizzard grinding

teacher.key_rationale: Both cud chewing (re-chewing regurgitated, partly digested grass) and gizzard grinding (muscular walls plus grit, in place of teeth) are specialised adaptations, not the same process as human chewing, so both rows are ✓, giving A. Options B, C and D each drop one or both stated conditions, marking an adaptation as if it were ordinary chewing.
